new.title: Climb Kahramanmaraş Castle for views over the city
new.desc: The hilltop castle above old Maraş was damaged in the February 2023 earthquakes and reopened to visitors after restoration. It overlooks the city centre and the plain towards the Ahır mountains.
new.tip: Go late afternoon for the best light; check current opening hours locally.
new.q: Kahramanmaraş Kalesi, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Visit the restored Ulu Cami of Kahramanmaraş
new.desc: The Ulu Cami, a roughly 600-year-old Dulkadirid-era mosque, was heavily damaged in 2023 and lost its minaret and entrance section. After restoration it reopened for worship on the Night of Power in March 2026.
new.tip: Dress modestly and avoid prayer times; it sits beside the rebuilt Kapalı Çarşı.
new.q: Kahramanmaraş Ulu Camii, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: See the Maraş elephant skeletons at the Archaeology Museum
new.desc: Founded in 1994, the Kahramanmaraş Archaeology Museum is known for ancient elephant skeletons ('Maraş Fili'), finds from Domuztepe mound and mosaics from Germanicia. It reopened after earthquake restoration.
new.tip: Allow an hour; opening hours and tickets are listed on the Ministry of Culture museum page.
new.q: Kahramanmaraş Arkeoloji Müzesi, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Walk among the mosaics of ancient Germanicia
new.desc: Germanicia, the Roman and Byzantine predecessor of Maraş, came to light in 2007 after looting at a site that now shows mosaic floors under protective cover. It was opened to visitors in 2018 and new mosaics keep being excavated.
new.tip: Combine it with the Archaeology Museum; bring water as shade is limited.
new.q: Germanicia Antik Kenti, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Browse the rebuilt Kapalı Çarşı for Maraş biber and tarhana
new.desc: The 500-year-old covered bazaar, wrecked in 2023, reopened after restoration of about 140 shops that had spent years trading from containers. It is the place to buy Maraş pul biber, tarhana, firik and copperware.
new.tip: Go in the morning; taste the pul biber before buying and ask for fresh tarhana.
new.q: Kahramanmaraş Kapalı Çarşı, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Eat Maraş dondurması at Yaşar Pastanesi
new.desc: Yaşar Pastanesi on Trabzon Caddesi began in the 1960s and grew into the Mado brand. It serves the stretchy, knife-cut goat-milk and salep Maraş ice cream.
new.tip: Order it plain or with cream; eat it with a knife and fork.
new.q: Yaşar Pastanesi, Trabzon Caddesi, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Eat home-style Maraş dishes at Küçük Ev Et Lokantası
new.desc: A home-style restaurant known for traditional Maraş dishes such as ekşili aya sulusu and sömelek köfte.
new.tip: Try the sömelek köfte or the ekşili dishes if available.
new.q: Küçük Ev Et Lokantası, Borsa Caddesi, İsmet Paşa Mahallesi, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Visit the Seven Sleepers cave at Eshab-ı Kehf
new.desc: The Eshab-ı Kehf complex near Afşin is built around a cave traditionally identified with the Seven Sleepers of the Quran's Kehf sura. It is on UNESCO's Tentative List and was restored for visitors.
new.tip: Local municipality guides can show you around; allow an hour or two.
new.q: Eshab-ı Kehf Külliyesi, Afşin, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: See the turquoise spring pond at Yeşilgöz
new.desc: Yeşilgöz is a spring-fed sinkhole pond in Tekir, on the Göksun road, whose water shifts between turquoise and emerald. The spring dried up and then clouded after the 2023 earthquake and has since largely recovered.
new.tip: Allow a picnic stop on the way to Göksun; water colour varies by season.
new.q: Yeşilgöz Mesire Alanı, Tekir, Onikişubat, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Look over Menzelet Dam from the Ali Kayası glass terrace
new.desc: A glass viewing terrace in Bulutoğlu hangs about 160 m above the Menzelet dam lake on the Ceyhan, with views of Güredil Castle. It has a restaurant and walking paths.
new.tip: Summer boat tours run on the lake below.
new.q: Ali Kayası Cam Terası, Bulutoğlu, Onikişubat, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Ski or hike on Ahır Dağı at Yedikuyular
new.desc: Yedikuyular Ski Resort lies on Ahır Mountain about 20 km northeast of Kahramanmaraş, with a T-bar and tow lifts. In summer the open slopes can be hiked towards the summit of Milcan Tepesi.
new.tip: Ski season is roughly December to March; check snow before driving up.
new.q: Yedikuyular Kayak Merkezi, Ulutaş, Dulkadiroğlu, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Escape the heat on the Başkonuş Plateau
new.desc: A highland at about 1,320 m popular for picnics, walking, camping and ATV tours, roughly 45 minutes from the city.
new.tip: Best in summer when Kahramanmaraş is hot; bring a picnic.
new.q: Başkonuş Yaylası, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Walk among old cedars at Yavşan Plateau Nature Park
new.desc: Yavşan Yaylası Tabiat Parkı sits at about 1,600 m, 36 km from the city, with cedars said to be 600 to 700 years old and endemic plants. It became a nature park in 2007.
new.tip: A vehicle entry fee applies; bring warm layers.
new.q: Yavşan Yaylası Tabiat Parkı, Onikişubat, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Visit the Seljuk-era Ulu Cami of Elbistan
new.desc: Elbistan's Ulu Cami is described as one of the district's most important historic buildings, a surviving Seljuk-era legacy in Güneşli neighbourhood.
new.tip: Check locally that it is open after the earthquakes; visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Elbistan Ulu Camii, Güneşli, Elbistan, Kahramanmaraş

new.title: Climb Ravanda Castle above the Afrin stream
new.desc: Ravanda Castle stands on a steep hill at Belenözü village in Polateli. A restored stair walkway, signs and benches lead up, and a legend says its cisterns link to a path to the Afrin stream.
new.tip: Free entry; take a dolmuş from Kilis to Polateli then Belenözü, or a taxi.
new.q: Ravanda Kalesi, Belenözü, Polateli, Kilis

new.title: Tour the Kilis Museum in the Neşet Efendi mansion
new.desc: The museum opened in 2012 inside the Neşet Efendi Konağı, a mansion built in 1925–27. It has archaeology and ethnography sections.
new.tip: Closed days vary; check hours before going.
new.q: Kilis Müzesi, Neşet Efendi Konağı, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Step into the Alaeddin Yavaşca Museum in Kilis
new.desc: A 1910-11 house in Tekye quarter, east of Cumhuriyet Square, opened as a museum in 2022 with 143 personal items of the composer and doctor Alaeddin Yavaşca. It is free and closed on Mondays.
new.tip: Open 08:30-17:00; it is close to the Mevlevi lodge, so combine the two.
new.q: Alaeddin Yavaşca Müzesi, Mevlevihane Sokak, Tekye Mahallesi, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Admire Canpolat Paşa Mosque, a Sinan-style landmark
new.desc: Kilis's most important Ottoman mosque, with an inscription dated 1553 naming Canbolat Bey. Attributed to Sinan's team though unproven, it resembles the Hüsreviye Mosque in Aleppo.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.
new.q: Canpolat Paşa Camii, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: See the courtyard and seven-jet fountain at Kilis Ulu Cami
new.desc: Kilis's largest mosque, with a wide courtyard, two entrances and a seven-spout fountain fed by Kurtağa stream water. Sources date it differently but agree it is the city's oldest.
new.tip: Free; avoid prayer times.
new.q: Kilis Ulu Camii, Hacı Gümüş Mahallesi, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Walk the Bronze Age mound of Oylum Höyük
new.desc: Oylum Höyük is one of the largest mounds in the Middle East, with settlement from the Late Chalcolithic onwards and excavations since 1989. A 6th-century mosaic basilica lies south-west of it.
new.tip: Open-air site; bring water and sun protection.
new.q: Oylum Höyük, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Eat Kilis tava at Tavacı İzzet Usta
new.desc: Kilis tava is a geographically-indicated minced-meat dish baked in a tray with aubergine and tomatoes. İzzet Usta is among the places named for it.
new.tip: Order Kilis tava with ayran; expect about 220 TL per portion.
new.q: Tavacı İzzet Usta, Abidin Ağa Caddesi, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Order Kilis katmer and cennet çamuru at Bekan Katmer
new.desc: Bekan Katmer is a salon known for Kilis katmer and the local sweet cennet çamuru.
new.tip: Go for breakfast or an afternoon dessert.
new.q: Bekan Katmer, Kilis Merkez, Kilis

new.title: Explore the ancient site of Belkıs-Zeugma on the Euphrates
new.desc: Zeugma, a Roman city on the Euphrates in Belkıs village, Nizip, minted its own coins and spreads over about 20,000 decares. Most mosaics are in the Zeugma Mosaic Museum in Gaziantep city.
new.tip: Check the Gaziantep culture office for current access to the excavation area.
new.q: Zeugma Antik Kenti, Belkıs, Nizip, Gaziantep

new.title: Reach the Euphrates fortress of Rumkale
new.desc: Rumkale, near Kasaba village in Yavuzeli, sits on a peninsula where the Merzimen river meets the Euphrates, with Roman and medieval remains. You approach by boat or via a glass terrace viewpoint.
new.tip: Boat trips run from Kasaba; summer weekends get busy.
new.q: Rumkale, Kasaba, Yavuzeli, Gaziantep

new.title: See unfinished Hittite statues at Yesemek
new.desc: Yesemek, about 20 km southeast of İslahiye, is the largest quarry and sculpture workshop of the Near East, active from the late 2nd millennium to the late 8th century BC. Hundreds of lions and sphinxes stand unfinished.
new.tip: Open-air; go in spring or autumn.
new.q: Yesemek Açık Hava Müzesi, İslahiye, Gaziantep

new.title: Visit the Mithras and Jupiter Dolichenus sanctuaries at Dülük
new.desc: Dülük is ancient Doliche, home of the cult of Jupiter Dolichenus; the sacred area on Dülük Baba Hill and an underground Mithraeum on Keber Hill have been excavated by Münster University.
new.tip: Check access with the Gaziantep culture office.
new.q: Dülük Antik Kenti, Şehitkamil, Gaziantep
